objetivo: That the student explains what reducing, reusing and recycling mean, gives examples of each, and understands how these habits reduce waste and take care of the environment.
hatsumon: What can we do with all the trash we make every day?

turnos.utterance_formal: Good morning. Come in, please, and leave your backpacks by the wall.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Good morning, okay, come in, come in, leave your backpacks by the wall.

turnos.utterance_formal: Today I brought something strange. It's a bag with the things from our classroom wastebasket from yesterday.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, today I brought something weird, eh. A bag with the stuff from our classroom wastebasket from yesterday.

turnos.utterance_formal: No, don't touch it, Pablo. I'll take things out one at a time.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: No, don't touch it, Pablo. I'll take stuff out one at a time, okay.

turnos.utterance_formal: This is a sheet of paper with a single line written on it. Is it trash? Should it be thrown away?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, this is a paper with, with just one line written on it. Is it trash? Should it be thrown away?

turnos.utterance_formal: Some of you say yes and some say no. And here's a plastic bottle, an apple core, and a juice box.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Some of you say yes, some say no. And here's a plastic bottle, an apple core and a juice box, see.

turnos.utterance_formal: Every one of us makes trash every day, and all of it has to go somewhere.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Every one of us makes trash every single day, and all of it has to go somewhere.

turnos.utterance_formal: Where does it go after the truck takes it? Yes, Camila, to a big dump, a landfill.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Where does it go after the truck takes it? Yes, Camila, to a big dump, a lan fill.

operations.text: Too much trash
Trash goes to big dumps called **landfills**, and they keep growing

turnos.utterance_formal: And the trash doesn't just disappear: a plastic bottle can take hundreds of years to break down.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the trash doesn't just disappear, eh: a plastic bottle takes hundreds of years to break down.

set.text: Trash goes to big dumps called **landfills**, and they keep growing. A plastic bottle takes hundreds of years to break down.

turnos.utterance_formal: But there are three things we can do before throwing something away: use less, use it again, or turn it into something new.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: But there are three things we can do before throwing something out: use less, use it again, or make something new from it.

operations.text: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's take them one by one. The first is to use less.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's go one by one. The first one is using less.

operations.text: Reduce
To **reduce** is to make less trash by using only what we need

turnos.utterance_formal: Who has a paper cup at home that you throw out after one use? Okay, a few of you.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Who's got those paper cups at home that you toss after one use? Okay, a few of you.

turnos.utterance_formal: If we bring our own water bottle every day, we don't need a new plastic bottle every day.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: If we bring our own water bottle every day, we don't need a new plastic bottle every day, right.

set.text: To **reduce** is to make less trash by using only what we need, for example by bringing our own water bottle.

turnos.utterance_formal: It's also good to carry a cloth bag to the market instead of getting a new plastic bag every time.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: It's also good to carry a cloth bag to the market, not take a new plastic bag every time.

turnos.utterance_formal: Isabel, you're laughing. Tell the whole class what's funny.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Isabel, you're laughing. Tell everyone what's so funny, go on.

turnos.utterance_formal: Her little brother uses so many napkins that the napkin pile is higher than his plate. Okay, okay, that's a good example of using more than we need.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Her little brother uses so many napkins the pile's higher than his plate. Okay, okay, good example of using more than you need.

operations.text: Taking only the napkins we need is also a way to reduce trash

turnos.utterance_formal: The second thing is to use something again instead of throwing it away.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The second one is to use something again instead of throwing it out.

operations.text: Reuse
To **reuse** is to use an object again, in the same way or in a new way

turnos.utterance_formal: A glass jar can hold pencils, and an old T-shirt can become a cleaning rag.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: A glass jar can hold pencils, and an old T shirt turns into a cleaning rag, you know.

operations.text:
glass jar as a pencil holder
old T-shirt as a rag
used paper as scratch paper

turnos.utterance_formal: What do you reuse at home? Raise your hand if your family uses the margarine tub for leftovers.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: What do you reuse at home? Hands up if your family keeps the margarine tub for leftovers.

operations.text: A margarine tub can keep leftovers

turnos.utterance_formal: Lucas says they plant flowers in old tires. Wow, that's something new for me.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Lucas says they plant flowers in old tires. Wow, that's new for me.

set.text: A margarine tub can keep leftovers, and old tires can become planters for flowers.

turnos.utterance_formal: The first sheet I showed you, the one with only a line, can be used on the back for drawing or notes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The first sheet I showed you, the one with one line, you can use the back for drawing or notes.

set.text: A margarine tub can keep leftovers, and old tires can become planters for flowers. A sheet written on one side can still be used on the back.

turnos.utterance_formal: So that sheet wasn't trash after all.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So that sheet wasn't trash after all, eh.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now the third thing, and probably the one you've heard the most: recycling.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now the third one, the one you've probably heard the most: re cy cling.

operations.text: Recycle
To **recycle** is to turn old materials into new products

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about a plastic bottle. In a recycling plant it is cleaned, ground into small pieces, and melted.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Think about a plastic bottle. At a recycling plant they clean it, grind it into little pieces and melt it.

turnos.utterance_formal: The melted plastic can become a bench, a bucket, or a new bottle.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The melted plastic can turn into a bench, a bucket or even a new bottle.

operations.text: Melted plastic can become a bench, a bucket or a new bottle

turnos.utterance_formal: Paper is also recycled: old paper is soaked in water to make a soft mush called pulp, and then it's pressed flat into new sheets.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Paper's recycled too: old paper is soaked in water into a soft mush called pulp, and then pressed flat into new sheets.

turnos.utterance_formal: Does anyone know where the paper at home comes from? Yes, Valeria, from trees.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Does anyone know where paper comes from? Yes, Valeria, from trees.

operations.text: Paper is made from trees

turnos.utterance_formal: Right, so each time we recycle paper we need to cut fewer trees.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Right, so every time we recycle paper we cut down fewer trees.

set.text: Paper is made from trees, so each time we recycle it fewer trees are cut down.

turnos.utterance_formal: Glass can be recycled too, again and again, without losing its quality.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Glass can be recycled too, again and again, and it doesn't lose quality.

set.text: Paper is made from trees, so each time we recycle it fewer trees are cut down. **Glass** can be melted and made into new glass again and again.

turnos.utterance_formal: Metal cans are melted too, and the metal is used to make new cans.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Metal cans, too, they get melted and the metal makes new cans, yes.

set.text: Paper is made from trees, so each time we recycle it fewer trees are cut down. **Glass** can be melted and made into new glass again and again. Metal cans are melted to make new cans.

turnos.utterance_formal: For this we need to separate our trash into groups: paper, plastic, glass, metal, and food scraps.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For that we have to sort our trash into groups: paper, plastic, glass, metal and food scraps.

operations.text:
paper
plastic
glass
metal
food scraps

turnos.utterance_formal: Wait, wait. I heard somebody say that the apple core goes with the plastic. Who said that? Thank you for being honest.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Wait, wait. I heard somebody say the apple core goes with the plastic. Who said that? Thanks for being honest.

turnos.utterance_formal: The apple core is organic waste. It rots and turns into compost, a rich soil for plants.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The apple core's organic, it rots and becomes compost, a rich soil for plants.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's a recycling too, a natural one.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's recycling too, a natural kind.

operations.text: Food scraps become **compost**, which helps plants grow.

turnos.utterance_formal: So how many things have we named so far? Three, exactly. Say them with me.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So how many have we named so far? Three, yeah. Say them with me.

turnos.utterance_formal: Reduce, reuse, and recycle.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Reduce, reuse, and, and recycle.

turnos.utterance_formal: Which one is best? The first one, because the best trash is the trash we never make.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Which one's best? The first, because the best trash is the one we never make.

operations.text: Which comes first
The best order is to **reduce** first, then reuse, and recycle last

turnos.utterance_formal: Why does this matter for the planet? Fewer things in landfills, less pollution, less water and energy used to make new things.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Why does this matter for the planet? Fewer things in landfills, less pollution, less water and energy to make new stuff.

operations.text:
Less trash in landfills
Less pollution
Less water and energy used

turnos.utterance_formal: Raise your hand if your family has already done one of these things this week.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Raise your hand if your family's already done one of these this week.

turnos.utterance_formal: Okay, quite a few. That makes me happy, truly.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, quite a few. That makes me real happy.

turnos.utterance_formal: So let's go back to the first question: what can we do with our trash?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So let's go back to the first question: what can we do with our trash?

turnos.utterance_formal: We use less of it, we use things more than once, and we turn the rest into something new.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We use less of it, we use things more than once, and we turn the rest into something new.

operations.text: We can **reduce** what we use, **reuse** what we have and **recycle** the rest.

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about the bottle: the bottle goes to the plant, and the plant makes something new.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Think about the bottle: the bottle goes to the plant, and the plant makes something new.

turnos.utterance_formal: And the paper does the same: old paper becomes pulp, and pulp becomes new paper.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the paper does the same: old paper becomes pulp, pulp becomes new paper.

turnos.utterance_formal: For tomorrow, think of one thing you can reduce, one you can reuse, and one you can recycle at home.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For tomorrow, think of one thing to reduce, one to reuse, one to recycle at home, okay.

operations.text: For tomorrow
Find one thing to reduce, one to reuse and one to recycle at home.

turnos.utterance_formal: Write them down in your notebook and share them with your family.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Put them in your notebook and tell your family.

set.text: Find one thing to reduce, one to reuse and one to recycle at home. Share them with your family.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now all together, please, let's pick up the paper on the floor and put it in the right bin.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now all together, let's pick up the paper from the floor and put it in the right bin.
